newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwanese ship said to put 12 stowaways overboard.
newsitem.headline: Taiwanese ship said to put 12 stowaways overboard.

text.p: Eleven Nigerian stowaways who said they were put off a Taiwanese trawler in mid-ocean have washed up on an island off the South African coast, a nature conservation spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman quoted the 11 as saying a 12th man had drowned after they were forced off the ship with oil drums to keep them afloat about three days ago.

They washed up on Tuesday night on Dyer Island, off the southernmost tip of the continent at Cape Agulhas. The island, which has important sea bird colonies, is permanently staffed by conservation officials.
"Dyer Island is also well known for its great white sharks, so they were quite lucky," the spokesman said.
A South African air force helicopter flew to the island on Wednesday to pick up the Nigerians.
